content: A dental auxiliary refers to any member of the dental team who supports the dentist in providing dental care. This group includes dental assistants, dental therapists, dental hygienists, and dental technicians. Their roles are typically defined and restricted by regional dental regulations, which establish the scope of treatments they are permitted to perform. Dental Assistants Dental assistants play a crucial role in improving the efficiency of dental treatments. They assist the dentist by holding and passing instruments, retracting tissues, and using suction devices to enhance visibility in the operating field. Additionally, they are responsible for mixing dental materials and maintaining accurate dental records. Dental Therapists Dental therapists are licensed professionals in certain countries who focus on treating children’s teeth and promoting oral hygiene. Their scope of practice is determined by local dental regulations. Under the supervision or prescription of a dentist, dental therapists are typically authorized to examine children’s teeth, administer specific types of local anesthesia, take radiographs, apply sealants, and perform scaling and cleaning procedures for children. They are also trained to restore primary teeth and carry out vital pulp treatments, such as pulpotomies. Dental Hygienists Dental hygienists are licensed professionals who specialize in preventive dental care, with a primary focus on oral hygiene techniques. Their responsibilities are defined by local dental regulations. In most regions, dental hygienists work under the supervision of a dentist. They are often licensed to administer certain types of local anesthesia, take radiographs, apply sealants, and perform scaling, root planing, and cleaning procedures. These tasks are aimed at maintaining and improving patients’ oral health. Dental Technicians Dental technicians are skilled professionals who create dental appliances for use by dentists. They fabricate removable prostheses, such as dentures, as well as fixed restorative devices, including crowns and bridges. These appliances are designed to be inserted by the dental operator during treatment.
